docs.text: Navigate to a directory quickly in Cursor (after SSH connection) When connected to a remote machine via SSH in Cursor, browsing folders through the file explorer can be slow. Instead, you can jump directly to directories using these methods. 1. Open a folder directly by path (recommended) Press: Ctrl + K then Ctrl + O (or go to File → Open Folder ) In the path field, type the absolute path : /home/ramesh/projects/k8s-operator or a relative path : ../configs Press Enter Cursor will immediately open that directory and show its structure in the explorer. 2. Use the Command Palette Press: Ctrl + Shift + P Type: File: Open Folder Enter the directory path and press Enter . 3. Navigate via terminal (fast if you know the path) Open the integrated terminal: `Ctrl + `` Navigate using: cd /home/ramesh/projects/operator Then open that directory as the workspace: cursor . 4. Jump to a file quickly If you know the file name but not its location: Press: Ctrl + P Then type the file name, for example: deployment.yaml Cursor will search the entire workspace and open the file. 5. Open a file using its path Press: Ctrl + P Then type something like: configs/envoy/envoy.yaml Cursor will jump directly to that file. Pro Tip Use Go to Symbol in Workspace to jump across code: Ctrl + T This allows you to navigate directly to functions, structs, variables, or symbols without browsing directories. Recommended workflow when using SSH with Cursor Ctrl + P → jump to files instantly Ctrl + K Ctrl + O → open folder by path Ctrl + T → jump to symbols across the workspace With these shortcuts, you rarely need to manually navigate through the directory tree.

docs.text: 3R Trading Framework A practical, disciplined approach to planning, executing, and holding 3R trades. What does 3R mean? R = Risk per trade 1R = the amount you are willing to lose on a trade 3R = profit equals 3 × risk Example: - Risk (1R) = ₹1,000 - 3R winner = ₹3,000 - 1R loss = −₹1,000 The goal is not high accuracy , but high-quality risk–reward . 1. DAILY 3R TRADE CHECKLIST Use this checklist before every trade . If even one item fails → NO TRADE . Market & Context [ ] Market is trending or clearly structured [ ] Trade direction aligns with higher timeframe trend [ ] Enough space till next support/resistance [ ] No major news event nearby Setup Quality [ ] Clear support / resistance / structure [ ] Entry near the level (not chasing) [ ] Stop-loss at invalidation , not random [ ] Stop-loss is reasonable (not extremely wide) Risk & Reward [ ] 1R (risk) predefined as % of capital [ ] Position size calculated from stop-loss [ ] 3R target is logical , not forced [ ] Target not blocked by a strong obstacle Psychology Check [ ] Calm state of mind [ ] Fully accept −1R loss [ ] Will not widen stop-loss [ ] Will wait for SL or target only 2. SAMPLE 3R TRADING PLAN Capital & Risk Capital: ₹2,00,000 Risk per trade: 0.5% 1R = ₹1,000 Max trades per day: 1–2 Max daily loss: −2R Market & Timeframe Market: Equity / Index Higher timeframe: Daily (trend) Entry timeframe: 15-min Strategy: Pullback to structure in trend Entry Rules Trade only in trend direction Entry near structure only No chasing fast candles Avoid entries after large no-wick candles Stop-Loss Rules Stop placed at idea invalidation Never widen stop SL hit = trade finished Target Rules Default target: 3R Partial booking allowed: 50% at 1.5R 50% at 3R No full exit before 2R unless structure breaks Trade Management After 2R → stop-loss to breakeven Trail only on structure breaks Ignore P&L during trade Review & Journal Journal every trade in R terms Weekly review: Average R Rule violations Emotional mistakes 3. BEGINNER-SAFE 2R → 3R TRANSITION PLAN Do not jump directly to 3R. Earn it step by step. Phase 1: Master 2R (Foundation) Duration: 20–30 trades Rules: - Fixed −1R stop - Fixed +2R target - No trailing - No partial exits Goal: - Discipline - Comfort holding winners Phase 2: Split Target Phase (Bridge) Duration: 15–20 trades Rules: - 50% book at 1.5R - 50% target at 3R - Stop to breakeven only after 2R Goal: - Reduce fear of giving back profits - Train patience Phase 3: Full 3R Execution Rules: - Default target = 3R - Partial booking only in choppy markets - Trail only after structure breaks Goal: - Fewer trades - Higher expectancy - Professional execution Regression Rule (Important) If you: - Cut winners early - Move stops emotionally - Feel anxiety holding trades ➡️ Return to Phase 2 This is normal and part of growth. Final Rules to Remember Risk first, reward later Structure decides, not emotions One good 3R trade can cover multiple losses Process > Outcome One-Line Summary 3R trading is not about making money fast — it’s about executing disciplined risk repeatedly.

docs.text: 📈 Bullish Engulfing at Daily Support A Practical Price Action Guide 1️⃣ What Is a Bullish Engulfing Candle A bullish engulfing candle occurs when: - A green (bullish) candle fully engulfs the body of the previous red (bearish) candle - Buyers overpower sellers completely What it means: Control shifts from sellers to buyers. 📌 The candle body matters more than the wick. 2️⃣ What “Daily Support” Really Means Daily support is not a single line , but a zone where price has reacted before. Strong daily support characteristics: Multiple historical touches Strong rejections (long lower wicks / impulsive green candles) Psychological levels (round numbers like 100, 500, 1000) 📌 Zones > exact prices. 3️⃣ Ideal Conditions for This Setup ✅ This setup works best when most of these align : 📍 Bullish engulfing forms at a daily support zone 📉 Prior trend was down or corrective 🕯️ Engulfing candle closes near its high 📊 Volume is higher than previous candles 🚫 No immediate resistance overhead If these conditions align → high probability trade 4️⃣ Entry Strategies 🔹 Conservative Entry (Safer) Enter above the high of the engulfing candle Confirms continuation 🔹 Aggressive Entry (Better R:R) Enter near 50% retracement of the engulfing candle Higher reward, higher risk 📌 Beginners should start with conservative entry . 5️⃣ Stop-Loss Placement (Mandatory) Choose one: Below the low of the engulfing candle Below the entire support zone (preferred) 📌 If price breaks support again → trade idea is invalid. 6️⃣ Target Planning 🎯 Always plan targets before entering . Target options: 🎯 Target 1: Nearest daily resistance / recent swing high 🎯 Target 2: 2R–3R (risk-to-reward) 🎯 Trail for trend continuation if structure supports it 📌 Never enter if upside space is limited. 7️⃣ Multi-Timeframe Confirmation (Pro Technique) Daily: Identify support + engulfing 15-min / 5-min: Higher low or consolidation 1-min: Breakout entry (optional) 📌 This filters many false engulfing signals. 8️⃣ When NOT to Trade This ❌ Avoid this setup when: Engulfing forms in sideways/choppy market Very low volume Strong resistance just above After a sharp, vertical fall (needs base first) During major news/events 9️⃣ Common Mistakes Traders Make Buying every engulfing candle blindly Ignoring higher timeframe resistance Placing stop-loss inside the support zone Expecting reversal immediately without confirmation 🧠 Pro Insight A bullish engulfing at daily support is not a buy signal It is permission to look for long trades ✅ Quick Checklist (Before Entry) [ ] At a clear daily support zone [ ] Prior down move or correction [ ] Strong engulfing close [ ] Acceptable volume [ ] Clear upside space [ ] Minimum 2R reward 📌 Best Use Case Swing trading Positional trades Intraday continuation using daily bias End of Document

docs.text: sync.WaitGroup in Go sync.WaitGroup is a synchronization primitive in Go used to wait for a collection of goroutines to finish executing . It is commonly used when: - launching multiple goroutines - you need to block until all of them complete - you do NOT need to return values directly (channels are used for that) Why WaitGroup is needed Goroutines run asynchronously. Without synchronization, the main function may exit before goroutines finish. go doWork() fmt.Println("main done") // may execute before doWork finishes Basic Usage Pattern var wg sync.WaitGroup wg.Add(1) go func() { defer wg.Done() // work here }() wg.Wait() Single GoRoutine package main import ( "fmt" "sync" ) func main() { var wg sync.WaitGroup wg.Add(1) go func() { defer wg.Done() fmt.Println("Hello from goroutine") }() wg.Wait() fmt.Println("All goroutines finished") } Multiple Goroutines var wg sync.WaitGroup for i := 0; i < 5; i++ { wg.Add(1) go func(i int) { defer wg.Done() fmt.Println("Worker", i) }(i) } wg.Wait() fmt.Println("All workers done") Waiting for Http Calls var wg sync.WaitGroup urls := []string{ "https://example.com", "https://golang.org", } for _, url := range urls { wg.Add(1) go func(u string) { defer wg.Done() fmt.Println("Fetching", u) }(url) } wg.Wait() WaitGroup with channels var wg sync.WaitGroup results := make(chan int, 5) for i := 0; i < 5; i++ { wg.Add(1) go func(i int) { defer wg.Done() results <- i * 2 }(i) } go func() { wg.Wait() close(results) }() for r := range results { fmt.Println("Result:", r) } Other details Do not call Add() inside goroutines go func() { wg.Add(1) // WRONG }() Use defer wg.Done() Ensures Done() is called even if the function returns early. Other Links [Go Official Docs] (https://pkg.go.dev/sync#WaitGroup)

docs.text: NSR in Kubernetes Contexts This document explains two possible interpretations of NSR in Kubernetes-related architectures: 1. NSR in Network Service Mesh 2. Container Registry usage in Kubernetes (if NSR was a misinterpretation) NSR within a Kubernetes Network Service Mesh In the Network Service Mesh (NSM) architecture, the NSR (also referred to as MSR – Mesh Service Registry ) acts as the central service discovery mechanism . Service Discovery The Kubernetes API server’s etcd is commonly leveraged as the backing store for the registry. It stores information about: Available network services Network Service Endpoints (NSEs) Associated metadata Registration Process NSMgr (Network Service Manager) runs as a control-plane component on each node. Its responsibilities include: Discovering local Network Service Endpoints (NSEs) Registering these NSEs with the NSR via the Kubernetes API server This ensures that all available services and endpoints are visible at the mesh level. Service Consumption A Network Service Client (NSC) , typically a Pod with specific annotations, requests a network service. The workflow is as follows: The local NSMgr receives the service request It queries the NSR (via the API server) for a suitable NSE A virtual wire (connection) is established between: The requesting client The selected Network Service Endpoint This enables dynamic, policy-driven service connectivity across the mesh. General Container Registry Usage in Kubernetes If “NSR” is a typo or misinterpretation and instead refers to the general concept of a container image registry in Kubernetes, the process is different and focuses on image distribution and authentication . Image Pulling The kubelet component on each node is responsible for pulling container images. It uses the configured container runtime, such as: Docker containerd CRI-O Images are pulled from a specified container registry. Authentication (Image Pull Secrets) For private container registries (for example: Docker Hub, AWS ECR, Azure Container Registry, Google Artifact Registry): A Kubernetes Secret of type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson must be created. This secret stores: Registry endpoint Authentication credentials Linking Secrets to Pods The image pull secret is referenced in the Pod specification. This allows the kubelet to authenticate with the registry and pull the required image. Example usage scenarios include: - Private enterprise registries - Cloud-provider-managed registries - Secured internal image repositories Summary In Network Service Mesh , NSR refers to a service registry used for discovering and connecting network services. In standard Kubernetes usage, registries are used for container image storage and distribution . These two concepts are unrelated but can be confused due to similar terminology. Understanding the context in which NSR is used is critical to interpreting its role correctly.

docs.text: 📙 docs/scheduling/node-affinity.md Node Affinity What is Node Affinity? Node Affinity is an advanced scheduling mechanism that allows expressive rules and preferences . A taint is applied to a node to repel Pods. key=value:effect Taint Effects NoSchedule Blocks new Pods Existing Pods stay running PreferNoSchedule Scheduler avoids the node if possible Not guaranteed (best-effort) NoExecute Evicts existing Pods Blocks new Pods ⚠️ NoExecute is the most dangerous taint effect and should be used with extreme caution.

docs.text: Git: Add a Folder Recursively This document explains how to add and commit an entire folder (including all subfolders and files) using Git. Add a Folder Recursively To stage all files and subdirectories inside a folder: git add path/to/folder/ This stages: All files inside src/ All nested subfolders and their contents Commit the Changes After staging, commit the folder: git commit -m "Add src folder recursively" Add All Files in the Repository (Optional) To stage everything in the current repository: git add . Then commit: git commit -m "Add all files recursively" Important Notes git add folder/ includes new and modified files git commit -am does NOT include new (untracked) files Always verify what will be committed: git status To preview staged changes: git diff --cached
docs.title: git-add-folder
